title: Horizontal Split Case Pump
model_title: Horizontal Split Case Pump (BB1, Double Suction)

introduction.definition: A horizontal split case pump has its casing divided on the horizontal plane through the shaft, with both nozzles in the lower half. A double-suction impeller between two bearings takes liquid from both sides, which lowers NPSH required and balances axial thrust. Removing the upper half exposes the whole rotor for inspection without disturbing pipework or motor.
key_points: Axially split casing: lift the top half to service the rotor
Double-suction impeller: low NPSHr and balanced thrust
Bearings at both ends: stiff rotor, long seal and bearing life
High flow, medium head; efficient in large sizes

classification.configuration: Between bearings, axially split, double suction

introduction.summary: A horizontal split case pump has its casing divided on the horizontal plane through the shaft centreline. The suction and discharge nozzles are cast into the lower half, so after removing the upper half the whole rotor (shaft, double-suction impeller, wear rings, sleeves, seals and bearings) can be lifted out without disturbing the pipework or the motor. Liquid from the side suction nozzle divides into two channels and enters the impeller from both sides; this halves the eye velocity (lower NPSH required) and balances the axial thrust. The impeller sits between two bearings, giving a stiff rotor suitable for large flows in water supply, cooling water, fire protection and pipeline service.

what_to_look_for: Liquid enters the side suction nozzle in the lower casing half.
Inside the casing the flow divides into two suction channels that feed the impeller from both sides.
The double-suction impeller accelerates both streams outward; equal and opposite eyes cancel most of the axial thrust.

steps.text: Liquid enters the side suction nozzle in the lower casing half.
Inside the casing the flow divides into two suction channels that feed the impeller from both sides.
The double-suction impeller accelerates both streams outward; equal and opposite eyes cancel most of the axial thrust.
Casing wear rings at both eyes limit internal leakage back to suction.
The volute collects the combined flow and converts velocity to pressure before the side discharge nozzle.
Seals at each shaft exit stop leakage; bearings outside both seals carry the rotor.
Removing the upper casing half exposes the complete rotor for inspection.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Stable rising-to-shut-off head curve; flat efficiency peak in large sizes; low NPSHr per unit flow thanks to double suction.

selection_notes: Use suction-side straight pipe so both eyes receive equal flow — elbows in the plane of the shaft cause uneven loading.
Check that the pump runs within its preferred operating region (ANSI/HI 9.6.3).

foundation: Rigid baseplate grouted on a concrete block; anchor bolts sized per the manufacturer.
alignment: Align pump and motor shafts with dial indicators or laser after grouting and again after connecting the piping (hot alignment check for hot service).
Target the coupling manufacturer's tolerances; typical practice for 1500–3000 rpm is ≤0.05 mm offset and ≤0.05 mm/100 mm angularity — verify.
Correct soft foot (< 0.05 mm) before final alignment.
piping: Support suction and discharge piping independently so nozzle loads stay within the manufacturer's (or API 610/HI 9.6.2) allowable values.
Provide a straight run of at least 5 pipe diameters ahead of the suction nozzle (ANSI/HI 9.6.6 guidance — verify) and use an eccentric reducer with the flat side up.
Fit isolation valves on both sides, a check valve on the discharge, and pressure gauges at suction and discharge.
Never use the pump as a pipe anchor; use expansion joints with tie rods only when designed for them.
Avoid an elbow in the horizontal plane directly at the suction nozzle — it feeds one eye more than the other (HI 9.6.6 — verify).
commissioning: Fill and vent the casing; never run dry.
Check rotation direction with the coupling disconnected.
Start against a partly open discharge valve, then open to the duty point; avoid running at shut-off.
Record baseline vibration, bearing temperature, suction and discharge pressure, flow and motor current.

routine.task: Check bearing temperature and vibration at both ends.
Check seal or gland leakage at both ends.

overhaul.task: Lift the upper casing; measure wear-ring clearances on both eyes.
Inspect impeller vanes and the volute cutwater for erosion or cavitation.
Replace the split-joint gasket with the correct thickness — a wrong gasket changes wear-ring fits.

lubrication: Oil-ring or grease lubricated rolling bearings; keep oil at the sight-glass mark.

symptoms: Damage on the pressure side of vane inlets
remedies: Operate within the preferred region; consider VFD or smaller impeller

causes: Elbow close to the suction nozzle in the shaft plane

remedies: Replace gasket; tighten in the specified sequence

causes: Sand or silt in raw water

video_tutorials.title: Horizontal Split Case Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Horizontal Split Case Pump.
Check bearing temperature and vibration at both ends.
Check seal or gland leakage at both ends.
Change bearing oil / regrease.
Check alignment and coupling condition.
Lift the upper casing; measure wear-ring clearances on both eyes.
Inspect impeller vanes and the volute cutwater for erosion or cavitation.
Watch for suction recirculation and cavitation: noise at low flow. Common cause: running well below bep.
Watch for unequal eye loading: higher axial thrust. Common cause: elbow close to the suction nozzle in the shaft plane.
Watch for split-joint leakage: weeping along the casing joint. Common cause: damaged gasket.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.

questions.question: Why does a double-suction impeller have a lower NPSH required than a single-suction impeller of the same flow?
options: Each eye handles only half the flow, so eye velocity is lower
questions.explanation: Half the flow per eye means lower inlet velocity and lower pressure drop at the vane inlets.

questions.question: What is the main maintenance advantage of the axially split casing?
options: The rotor can be inspected after lifting the upper half without disturbing the piping
questions.explanation: Both nozzles are in the lower half.

questions.question: Where are the bearings of a BB1 pump?
options: At both ends of the shaft, outside the casing
questions.explanation: Between-bearings design: one bearing housing at each end.

questions.question: An elbow in the plane of the shaft right at the suction nozzle can cause…
options: Unequal flow to the two eyes and extra axial thrust
questions.explanation: The two eyes must receive equal, uniform flow.

questions.question: Which API 610 code covers one- and two-stage axially split between-bearing pumps?
questions.explanation: BB = between bearings; BB1 = axially split 1–2 stage.
